title: Why are tennis balls yellow? The television connection

sources.name: International Tennis Federation — History of tennis balls

practice: Put your sporting curiosity to work with a mixed Sports Quiz.

sections.title: The colour was chosen for the viewers
sections.html:
Tennis balls became yellow because research found them easier for television viewers to see. Earlier balls were black or white, depending on the court background.

The International Tennis Federation’s history gives the reason. That bright blur is doing a job for the person on the sofa as well as the players on court.

sections.title: When did tennis balls turn yellow?
sections.html:
1972 and 1986 describe different changes:

  • 1972: the ITF introduced yellow balls into the rules of tennis.
  • 1986: Wimbledon adopted yellow balls after continuing with white ones.

Wimbledon’s museum learning pack confirms its later switch. The rule change did not turn every tournament yellow overnight.

sections.title: Would white balls in a 1980 clip be a mistake?
sections.html:
Not if it is Wimbledon. White balls fit that tournament’s timeline in 1980, six years before its switch. The colour alone would not prove an archive clip’s exact date, though.

Once you have spotted the ball, try reading the score from love to deuce. Both details make the next rally a little easier to follow.

description: Yellow tennis balls were easier to see on television. Discover why 1972 and Wimbledon’s 1986 change are both right, and what colour came before.
